neighbours.label: a verb or preposition set up to take an exhaustive object (impossible to discuss all..., checked against the whole list)
fire: There are so many dialects that no single book could hope to describe all of them.
It would take a lifetime to read every novel in this library.
In one short talk, it is impossible to cover all the changes in the new tax code.
Each new entry is compared against every record already stored in the database.
The inspector tried to visit all forty-two farms in the district in a single week.
No guidebook can list every restaurant worth trying in Tokyo.
The script validates each username against the full list of banned words.
She has been to nearly every national park in the United States.
quiet: There are two main dialects, and this short book describes the northern one.
It would take an afternoon to read this short novel from the library.
In one short talk, it is easy to explain the main change in the new tax code.
Each new entry is saved with the date and the name of the user.
The inspector visited the largest farm in the district on Tuesday.
This guidebook recommends a small noodle shop near the station in Tokyo.
The script prints each username in lowercase before saving the file.
She has been to Yellowstone twice with her grandparents.

predictions: Next-token-style pole: the verb after 'impossible to' / 'checked against' fires when the setup predicts 'all/every/the entire'; the same verbs with a narrow, specific object stay low.
notes: Probe: 'impossible in one article to discuss all' 0.612 vs 'easy in one article to discuss the main idea' 0.097; 'checked against the sales region' 0.363; 'almost every country' 0.299; 'until they have answered all' 0.212; 'Burning all recoverable coal' (sentence-initial verb) 0.081. Opposite pole promotes ' all', ' every', ' entire'.
